_comment: Where this directory comes from, machine-readable so `npm run check:vendored-parser` can hold
it to upstream: it fetches every file of the upstream directory at `tag` and compares bytes.
Nothing else may live here except `own_files`; a local-only file would shadow a copied one.
`allowed_divergences` is the ONE place a local edit is permitted, and each entry has to say
why and when it goes away. The checker substitutes `local` for `upstream` in the fetched file
before comparing, so the moment upstream changes that line the entry stops matching, the
check fails, and the shim gets removed rather than forgotten.
A newer upstream tag also fails the check: the copy is taken from a tagged release, and a
release we have not looked at is the event the reviewer asked to be told about.

allowed_divergences.why: TypeScript 4.0.8 (HyperFormula's) does not narrow `unknown` through `!== null && typeof === 'object'`; upstream compiles under ^5.9.3. One cast makes the file compile here. Semantics unchanged.
allowed_divergences.until: upstream ships the cast (or HyperFormula moves to TypeScript >= 4.9) - then delete this entry and re-take the file
allowed_divergences.local: Object.keys(current as object).forEach(key => pending.push((current as Record<string, unknown>)[key]));
